findings.title: Personal OAuth dispatch lacks the required ~/.claude LLM-egress boundary
findings.what: The design permits `personal-oauth` credentials with in-pod refresh and mounts the resolved credential into a general-purpose `claude -p` container. It applies ADR 0008 egress scrubbing only to `enterprise-api`; the sidecar allowlist at lines 502-510 governs telemetry sent to push-ingest, not content read by Claude and sent in subscription-authenticated LLM requests. Excluding seeded session history from the image likewise does not prevent runtime ~/.claude files from entering model context. Thus the required rule that a subscription OAuth credential must never send ~/.claude content is not enforced.
findings.fix: Require an explicit personal-OAuth execution boundary: do not mount or expose ~/.claude session/config content to the Claude process except the minimal credential material, enforce an allowlisted workspace for model-readable files, and add a fail-closed ADR 0008 egress scrub that rejects subscription-authenticated requests containing classified ~/.claude content.
findings.acceptance: An automated adversarial dispatch using `personal-oauth` creates sentinel files under each classified ~/.claude session/config path and attempts to include them in a model request; the outbound request is blocked or the sent payload is proven sentinel-free, while an ordinary workspace-only request succeeds. The test must separately prove that push-ingest filtering is not being mistaken for LLM-egress filtering.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the credential resolution, Job mounting, shipper filtering, and Vault paragraphs at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The only stated ADR 0008 egress governance is attached to `enterprise-api` at lines 473-478; lines 498-510 constrain the telemetry sidecar, and lines 532-534 explicitly carry the subscription OAuth seed into the MVP. No personal-OAuth LLM-egress exclusion is specified.
